solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: American hare finally caught by sailor and religious leader

parts.note: Jack, or Jack tar, is an old name for a sailor
a rabbi leads a Jewish congregation

indicators.note: says only the closing letter of the word caught is wanted

explanation.surface: A hare in America is at last captured by a sailor and a rabbi working together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American hare' is the whole definition; the jackrabbit is in fact a hare, not a rabbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackrabbit is a large long-eared hare of western North America.

clue.text: Early settler's source of fibre?

definitions.meaning: the ... were a Germanic people who settled in England in the 5th century
a plant whose fibre makes sacking and twine

explanation.surface: Where did the first settlers get their roughage?
explanation.walkthrough: 'fibre' suggests diet, but jute is a textile fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jutes arrived in Britain with the Angles and Saxons; jute the plant gives coarse fibre.

clue.text: Cat taking water in French country house

parts.note: chat is French for cat
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: A cat drinking water inside a French mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are French: CHAT for cat and EAU for water.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French castle or large country residence.

clue.text: Control plant, securing rebirth

parts.note: to rein in is to control
a carnation is a flowering plant

explanation.surface: Keeping a plant in check while making sure it grows anew.
explanation.definitionFit: Reincarnation is the soul's being born again in a new body.

clue.text: Red wine? Sounds like something a pugnacious type may pick

indicators.note: says the word is given as it is spoken rather than spelt

parts.words: something a pugnacious type may pick
parts.note: a quarrelsome person picks a bone, has a bone to pick

explanation.surface: A wine that a scrapper might choose.
explanation.walkthrough: To have a bone to pick is to have a grievance to air; 'Red wine?' with a query since Beaune is also a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaune is a Burgundy wine, often red, from around the town of that name.

clue.text: Lock up young man supporting African warriors without resistance

indicators.note: in a down clue the young man sits beneath, holding up the rest
used in the old sense of outside, so the warriors' letters go round the resistance

parts.note: an impi is a Zulu regiment of warriors; the word serves as its own plural
R is the physics symbol for resistance
a son is a young man, someone's boy

explanation.surface: Jail a youth who backs African fighters without putting up a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside: IMPI goes round R.
explanation.definitionFit: To lock up someone is to put them in prison, i.e. confine them.

clue.text: Vitality unknown in Grantchester at first

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities

indicators.note: asks for just the opening letter of the word Grantchester

explanation.surface: There is a mysterious liveliness in the Cambridgeshire village of Grantchester.
explanation.walkthrough: Z, then IN as written, then G from 'at first' on 'Grantchester'.
explanation.definitionFit: Zing is informal for energy, liveliness or zest, a synonym of vitality.

clue.text: Sloth I train somehow round back of menagerie

indicators.note: says the rearranged letters wrap about the letter from menagerie
says the letters of train are arranged in some other way
asks for the final letter of the word menagerie

explanation.surface: I teach a sloth somehow, circling the rear of the zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: NRTIA, the anagram of TRAIN, goes 'round' E, the 'back of' menagerie, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is sluggishness or reluctance to act, the vice of sloth.

clue.text: Good university man finally controlling smuggling racket

indicators.note: asks for only the last letter of the word man

parts.note: running means managing or controlling

explanation.surface: A decent graduate who ends up in charge of a contraband ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunrunning is the illegal trafficking of firearms, a smuggling operation.

clue.text: Ruler way back, initially named in song

indicators.note: tells us the abbreviation for way is read in the backward direction

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: tells us the initial letter goes inside the word for song

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera

indicators.note: asks for only the opening letter of the word named

explanation.surface: A ruler from long ago was first mentioned in a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruler way back' tempts as the definition of an ancient monarch; 'way back' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the empress of Russia, a female sovereign or ruler.

clue.text: Part of horse's behind associated with power

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
astern means behind, at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Something about a horse's rear end being linked with strength.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the horse's rump, but 'behind' is ASTERN and the definition is just 'Part of horse's', a part of a horse's leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The pastern is the section of a horse's foot between the fetlock and the hoof.

clue.text: Streets around Essex town by which one means to progress

indicators.note: says the streets surround the town's name

parts.note: St is short for street, so two streets give two of them
Epping is a town in Essex
taken as written

explanation.surface: Roads circle a town in Essex, through which someone gets ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is a county east of London; 'by which' links ONE to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepping stone is a stage or stepping point that helps one advance.

clue.text: Like trade involving churchgoer in shabby headgear

indicators.note: says the churchgoer's letters are placed within the words for shabby headgear

parts.note: mean can describe something shabby or squalid
RC stands for Roman Catholic, a churchgoer
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A commercial matter concerning a worshipper wearing a tatty hat.
explanation.walkthrough: TILE for a hat is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercantile means relating to merchants and commerce, so it describes trade.

clue.text: Mostly tense character in Euripides, say?

indicators.note: says the word for tense loses its final letter

parts.note: taut means stretched tight or tense

explanation.surface: A nervy figure from a Greek tragedy, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like a person in a play, but it means a letter; Euripides wrote in Greek, hence 'say?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet, the script in which Euripides wrote.

clue.text: Sadly my team's mostly fat and unbalanced

indicators.note: says the words my team's are jumbled, things going badly for them
says the word for fat loses its last letter

parts.note: rich food is fatty

explanation.surface: Unfortunately my side are mostly overweight and lopsided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' gives ASYMMET from MY TEAM'S; 'mostly' trims RICH to RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Asymmetric means lacking symmetry, so lopsided or not evenly balanced.

clue.text: Move fast, wanting second hot dish

parts.note: a curry is a spicy hot dish

explanation.surface: Someone hurries off, wanting a second helping of a spicy meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To scurry is to hurry along with short quick steps.

clue.text: Fellow politician in US city first to gripe

indicators.note: says the city's letters come before the word in rather than after it

parts.note: co- as a prefix means fellow, as in co-worker
MP is a Member of Parliament
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A fellow politician in an American city is the first to grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow politician' reads as a colleague, but the two words give separate pieces; 'first' reorders the last two.
explanation.definitionFit: To gripe is to grumble or protest, a synonym of complain.

clue.text: Where a flyer may go for a walk in London?

definitions.text: Where a flyer may go for a walk in London?

parts.words: Where a flyer may go for a walk in London?
parts.note: a flyer here is a bird, kept in a cage, and the second reading is a street of that name by St James's Park in London

explanation.surface: Where a pilot might stroll in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyer' suggests a pilot, but it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet bird lives in a cage, and Birdcage Walk is a well-known London street near Buckingham Palace.

clue.text: High official's valet endlessly taking risks

parts.note: a man is a manservant or valet

indicators.note: says the word for taking risks loses its final letter

parts.note: daring means bold, taking risks

explanation.surface: A senior official's servant keeps taking chances.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin was a senior official in imperial China, now any powerful bureaucrat.

clue.text: Relating to river — nothing to do with ears!

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero
otic means relating to the ear

explanation.surface: Something about a river that, oddly, has nothing to do with hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface denies any link to ears, but 'to do with ears' is OTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Nilotic means of the Nile, the river, or its region and peoples.

clue.text: Agreement thus broken ultimately by academic institution

parts.note: uni is short for university
so means thus, in this way

indicators.note: asks only for the final letter of the word broken

explanation.surface: A deal is thereby wrecked in the end by a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives N, the last letter of 'broken'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means in complete accord, so it means agreement.

clue.text: Endurance shown by southern girl touring America

indicators.note: says the girl travels all round the abbreviation for America

parts.note: Tina is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Staying power displayed by a girl from the south on a trip across America.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is the physical or mental strength to keep going, i.e. staying power.

clue.text: Demons one youngster encountered in Northern Ireland

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: says the youngster sits within the abbreviation for Northern Ireland

parts.note: a cub is a young animal or young person

explanation.surface: Evil spirits that a lone child came across in Ulster.
explanation.definitionFit: Incubi are male demons said to visit sleeping women.

clue.text: Old unit of measurement some levellers used

indicators.note: says only part of the word levellers is used, the run of letters lying in it

explanation.surface: An old measure that some of the Levellers, the radical group, once used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' points to a run of letters inside 'levellers'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ell was an old English measure of cloth length, about 45 inches.

clue.text: Popular Welsh girl entertaining accomplished islander

indicators.note: says the popular Welsh girl holds the word for accomplished inside, as a host holds guests

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Sian is a Welsh girl's name
done means completed or accomplished

explanation.surface: A well-liked Welsh woman plays host to a skilled visitor from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accomplished' looks like praise for the islander, but it is the inserted piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is an island nation, so an Indonesian is an islander.

clue.text: Joint head of kindergarten born in Paris

indicators.note: asks for the opening letter of the word kindergarten

parts.note: née is French for born, used for a married woman's maiden name

explanation.surface: The leader of a nursery school was born in the French capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the joint between the thigh and the lower leg.

clue.text: Decay reported beneath the Pantheon, for example

parts.note: rot means decay

indicators.note: says the word for beneath is given as it is spoken, with the final r unsounded

parts.note: under means beneath

explanation.surface: Rot has been found under the famous Roman temple.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent UNDER sounds like UNDA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pantheon in Rome is a circular domed building, which is what a rotunda is.

clue.text: Ideal cover secured by upper-class Scotsman

indicators.note: says the word for cover is held between the other pieces

parts.note: U is the label for upper-class usage
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name
a top is a lid or cover

explanation.surface: A perfect hiding place is provided by a posh Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopian describes an imagined perfect society, hence idealised or ideal.

clue.text: Firm originally cultivating a South American shrub

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: asks for just the opening letter of the word cultivating

explanation.surface: A company that started by growing a plant from South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Coca is an Andean bush whose leaves are the source of cocaine.

clue.text: Remove freedom, as it were, to take counsel

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as ..., the opposite of setting free

explanation.surface: Restricting liberty, so to speak, in order to seek advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it were' flags the punning first sense: DE- undoes LIBERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberate is to discuss or weigh up a matter, as when consulting others.
